issues.description: Command names inconsistent with sibling commands (quickmark_save, bookmark_add use singular; new ones use plural)
issues.detail: The file already uses `quickmark_save`, `quickmark_load`, `bookmark_add`, `bookmark_load` — singular noun, underscore verb. The new commands use `quickmarks_reload` / `bookmarks_reload`. That's two different naming conventions complecting in one dispatcher. Pick one. The simple choice: match the neighbors as `quickmark_reload` / `bookmark_reload`.

issues.description: reload() silently swallows file-read and parse errors that __init__ surfaces via _init_lineparser/_parse_line
issues.detail: In __init__, parse errors raised by _parse_line propagate to startup where the user sees them. After this change, the same path runs at runtime on a user command with no try/except and no user feedback distinguishing success from partial failure. The 'Bookmarks reloaded.' message will be shown even when a malformed line raised mid-iteration. Time semantics of error handling changed; make it explicit.

issues.description: reload() is not atomic: marks are cleared before the new file is read, so a read failure leaves the in-memory state empty
issues.detail: The value the user cares about is 'the set of marks'. reload() destroys that value first, then attempts to rebuild it from disk. If _init_lineparser or iteration fails, the user is left with no marks and a changed signal already pending emission. Build the new OrderedDict from disk first, then swap. Value semantics, not place-oriented mutation.

issues.description: Parsing logic duplicated conceptually between __init__ flow and reload() — extract a pure load_from_lineparser
issues.detail: The loop (skip blanks/comments, _parse_line) is the actual essence; clear+emit is the identity-update wrapper. A small pure function `_load_marks(lineparser) -> OrderedDict` separates the value (parsed marks) from the identity update (assign + emit). __init__ and reload both call it. Same code, less complecting of 'parse' with 'mutate self'.

issues.description: changed signal now fires during __init__ where it previously did not
issues.detail: Old __init__ populated self.marks directly and never emitted changed. New __init__ calls reload(), which emits changed at construction time before _init_savemanager runs. Any listener wired up before construction completes (or via objreg lookups during init order) sees a changed event for an empty-then-filled transition that didn't exist before. Verify no subscriber assumes 'no changed during startup'.

issues.description: feature-test scenarios are unnamed and don't restore prior state between scenarios
issues.detail: Both new Gherkin scenarios omit a title ('Scenario:' with no name) — easy to miss in test output, hard to grep. They also only assert the message string, not that reload actually re-read the file. A scenario that writes a new entry to the file then runs :bookmarks-reload then asserts the new entry is present would test the actual behavior, not just the success message.

review.summary: The feature is small and the intent is sound: expose the existing parse-loop as a callable so it can run twice. The decomposition into `reload()` is the right move and the unit test is honest. But the implementation complects three concerns — clearing identity, reading disk, and emitting change — in a single non-atomic mutation, so a parse error mid-reload silently wipes the user's marks while the UI says "reloaded." Command names also fork from the existing singular convention in the same file. Decompose `_load_marks(lineparser) -> OrderedDict` as a pure step, swap identity once, then emit; and align the command names with their neighbors.
